title: optimize-recs-playbook-grooming
body:
Purpose and audience:

This is a lightweight playbook + grooming record for the Optimize recommendations UI: the surface that suggests batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles to customers based on observed workload traces. Primary audience: product manager (optimize), UX, applied-ml, and eng owners for runtime and console.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Increase adoption of suggested recommendations by 20% for customers on hosted API within 12 weeks of rollout.
- Reduce average cost-per-token for participating routes by 15% via batching/caching changes without degrading P99 latency beyond SLA.
- Provide clear explanation for each suggestion so SRE/engineers can evaluate risk before applying.

High-level user journeys: (three top-level personas)
1) Growth engineer (PLG customer)
   - Land in Console -> Routes -> Route detail -> Optimizations tab -> Sees prioritized suggestions (Batch size, Cache TTL, Quantize to Q4_8) -> Preview impact (estimated cost saving, latency delta) -> Apply -> Request is sent to Dedicated/Hosted config -> changes staged & monitored.
2) Platform engineer (enterprise)
   - Bulk review for multiple routes -> Filter by model, region, SLAs -> Make canary rollout plan using rollout controls -> Audit log entry and approval required.
3) Evaluator (SRE/product)
   - Inspect why the suggestion was made: link to the sample trace, token distribution histogram, peak qps windows, and a diff view of model output (quality regression estimate).

Wireframe notes (low-fidelity/for grooming):
- Main card list (left column) with suggestion types and prioritization score (Savings x Confidence). Each card includes: short title, primary metric (est. $/day saved), confidence badge (High/Med/Low), and quick actions (preview, apply, ignore).
- Right panel: deep inspect view for selected suggestion. Tabs: "Why this" (trace snippet + feature importance), "Impact" (cost, latency, quality risk), "Preview" (simulated traffic baseline vs proposed), "Audit & Rollout" (approval flow).
- Top-level header shows route summary (model, average seq length, typical batch size, current quant profile) and quick toggles to switch environment (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Small inline visuals: histogram of sequence lengths, cumulative cost-by-token chart, KV cache hit-rate over time, per-token latency CDF.

Suggested copy snippets (for designers/devs to iterate):
- Suggestion headline: "Enable prefix caching (TTL 30s) — est. 12% cost reduction"
- Why: "Repeated prompts detected across multiple users during the 10:00–12:00 window; caching could avoid repeated decoder work for the common prefixes."
- Preview CTA: "Run simulated 1-hour replay"
- Apply CTA (with microcopy): "Apply to route — create canary (10% traffic)"

Recommendation heuristics (how suggestions are generated) — grooming notes, not final algos:
- Batching suggestion heuristic:
  - If average latency < SLO and tail utilization < 80% and median batch occupancy < (max_batch * 0.7) but there is strong inter-request arrival clustering in 200ms windows -> suggest increasing target batch size or enabling request coalescing.
- Caching suggestion heuristic:
  - If identical prefix ratio > 6% and avg RL prefix length > 8 tokens and hit-rate modeling projects > 5% token-level savings -> suggest prefix cache with TTL tuned by user activity window.
- Quantization suggestion heuristic:
  - If model variant has quantized profile validated in lab for this workload and quality regression estimate (ROUGE/embedding drift) < threshold -> propose profile (e.g., int8-ggml or q4_0) with estimated latency/cost impact and rollback plan.

Quality regression estimation (talking points for applied-ml):
- Use stratified prompt sampling across top-10 most frequent prompts for the route; compute embedding-distance drift and LM-logprob shifts. Present both an automated "quality risk" badge and the raw sample diffs.
- For sensitive routes (tagged "safety-critical"), require manual review AND include an A/B compare session with side-by-side outputs.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI shows up to 10 prioritized suggestions per route with correct estimated savings numbers (within ±15% of simulation).
- Deep-inspect view surfaces trace snippet and at least two visualizations (seq-length histogram, cache-hit projection).
- "Apply" path creates a canary change with explicit rollback request and writes an audit log entry.
- Suggestions include a confidence level and link to the underlying artifacts (trace id, simulation job id).

Backlog (groomed items, rough sizing):
- OPT-201: Implement suggestion card list component (FE) — 3 points — owner: Priya.
- OPT-202: Backend endpoint to generate previews via 1-hour simulated replay — 5 points — owner: Ivan.
- OPT-203: Trace visualizations library (CDF/histogram components) + sample trace export — 3 points — owner: Marco.
- OPT-204: Apply-canary pipeline + audit-log integration + policy checks for enterprise routes — 8 points — owner: Eng-Platform.
- OPT-205: Quantization profile safety tests and automatic regression scoring — 5 points — owner: Applied-ML.
- OPT-206: UX copy + accessibility pass (ARIA live regions for simulation results) — 2 points — owner: Design.

Risks and open questions (for the next grooming session):
- Simulation fidelity vs cost: How cheap/fast can we run previews without wasting infra? Can we sample or run approximate sims?
- Data privacy: For private deployments we cannot export traces to hosted preview jobs — must run there or provide a shim.
- Rollout default: Should the "Apply" CTA default to canary or full? (Recommend default canary, enterprise opt-in for full).
- Metric alignment: Which cost model should the UI surface? Token-charge-only or include infra amortized costs? Need finance input.

Proposed next steps (owners & timeline):
- This week: Align on acceptance criteria with SRE and Applied-ML (Sasha) — due 2024-11-15.
- 2-week sprint: FE skeleton + backend preview endpoint stub (Priya & Ivan) — due 2024-11-29.
- Post-sprint: Internal alpha with 3 pilot customers (no auto-apply) — target 2024-12-20.

Notes to reviewers:
- Prioritize explainability over aggressive automation. Engineers must be able to reproduce the rationale from traces.
- Keep the first shipped set to batching + caching; quantization can be opt-in once safety/regression signals are stable.
- Tag any UX mocks with "optimize-alpha" in Figma and link to this doc.

Scratchpad (raw fragments from sync):
- "Could we show a slider for canary % when applying?" -> yes, add to small enhancements list.
- "Confidence score should combine model-fit + replay variance" -> Ivan to propose formula.
- "Potential to tie suggestions to billing alerts" -> backlog item.

Related links and references:
- Previous wireframes in this folder (see: optimize-suggestion-canvas-ux-draft) but this doc focuses on operational playbook and acceptance criteria.
- Slack thread: #optimize-suggestions (link above).

Tagged owners and reviewers: @Priya Desai (UX), @Ivan Lopez (Eng), @Marco Nguyen (Applied-ML), @Sasha Kim (PM).
